title: Drop-In sessions meant to calm fears about changes coming to Wave Transit System
text:
The ladies sitting at the same table at the Thomas Sullivan Community Center have at least two things in common.They all ride the bus.And they all are concerned
"The Wave" riders met with staff to voice concerns about upcoming changes to the bus system. Two more public meetings are scheduled for this week.
The ladies sitting at the same table at the Thomas Sullivan Community Center have at least two things in common.
"This is not a good plan," said Amilia Moore. "This is not a good plan. ""I love my job," she says. "I've been working there for 30 years.
" She and the others at this table came to the center to hear about the city's plan to rebrand and realign the Wave Transit System. "It's inconvenient," says Amilia. "They're going the wrong way. " "It was called Mobile Transit first...
Authority...
" pipes up another woman, "and then they went to Wave. "She raised two kids while riding the bus... and she still does. "I'm used to riding like Dauphin Island Parkway to Mobile. And when I get down here to Mobile, and when I get down here to the GM&O, I get on the one I want and go.
And not have to get on the phone and call someone and say come get me or take me here or there. No. This new thing, it's not doing it.
"Some of the routes may change soon, but Via, the company that is operating the system for the city, says microtransit is a service that connects people to the transit system... customers that might be more than a quick walk away from a bus stop or route. "So micro transit is going to look a little bit differently, says The Wave Transit manager Lexie Trinkle, "but it's going to be what we look like as a minivan maybe or a suburban, things like that.
Smaller vehicle, it's a little bit more efficient, a little bit faster, and that's going to be replacing, in some cases, that city bus.
"But when the system becomes Second Line Transit in July, it will increase its use of microtransiting. "So, any bus stop that was considered a stop today is still going to be covered by public transit," says Trinkle. "It's just going to be covered by maybe a fixed line or maybe micro transit. "It's new, and it's different, and these riders are suspicious of it.
"You gotta say yes, no, one, two or three on the phone and stuff," worries rider Pamela McGadden. "A lot of seniors don't know. " The revamped service won't go into effect until July... which is why Trinkle says her transit system staff is holding these drop-in sessions now. "What we're wanting to do now is get in, take feedback, give an opportunity for a voice to be heard.
"There are two more drop-in information sessions scheduled this week in Mobile... Thursday from 3:30 to 6:30 at the West Regional Library on Grelot Rd, and Friday from 11:30 until 2 at the Ben May Main Library downtown.
